email.subject: Your parcel is on its way

body.v: Your parcel has left our depot and will be delivered tomorrow. You do not need to do anything.
You can also follow it in the ParcelPoint app.

hotspots.explain: The address is on parcelpoint.example, the company's real domain.
No deadline and no payment. It only tells you what is happening.
The link leads to parcelpoint.example, the real domain. Even so, the app is the safest way to look.
It points you to the app, a channel you already control.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: ParcelPoint itself: the address is on parcelpoint.example and the spelling is clean.
choices: A scammer using a lookalike address
A stranger with a free mailbox

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: None. It is a calm update with no deadline.
choices: None: it is a calm update

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Nothing. It only tells you the parcel is on its way and offers a tracking link.

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: You do not need to act. If you want to look, open the ParcelPoint app yourself.
choices: Open the ParcelPoint app yourself if you want to look
Forward it to a friend to check

actions.label: Open the ParcelPoint app yourself if you want to check
actions.consequence: You see the same delivery date. Nothing was needed.

actions.label: Do nothing and wait for the parcel
actions.consequence: The parcel arrives tomorrow. Nothing was needed.

actions.label: Reply with your home address, just in case
actions.consequence: The no-reply address does not answer. You gave away nothing useful, but nothing was needed either.

attacker_reveal: This one is real, dear. It comes from the company's own domain, asks for nothing and has no deadline. A parcel notice that only informs you is exactly what a real one looks like.
